title: Hopper FP8 profiling corridor and noise-tolerant activation reconciler
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: enable stable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) rollouts on Hopper by building a profiling corridor for activation statistics, a noise-tolerant activation reconciler to reduce spurious drift signals, and an orchestrated calibration flow that feeds the runtime selector. This ticket ties profiling, synthetic calibration generation, drift detection hardening, and canary shadow sampling into a single deliverable so we can increase activation rate safely and reduce rollback churn.

Scope:
- Implement a lightweight profiling corridor that captures per-layer activation distribution quantiles (p1/p5/median/p95/p99) and prefix KV norms during shadow runs.
- Develop an activation reconciler that applies smoothing, noise floor clipping, and per-layer hysteresis before triggering a gateway-level fallback to INT8/FP16.
- Integrate the corridor output into the calibration orchestrator so candidate E4M3/E5M2 profiles are scored by stability and worst-case deviation.
- Add golden-suite checks and a small synthetic perturbation harness to ensure drift-tolerant behavior under token distribution skews.
- Wire telemetry and SLO gating for canary sampling and automated rollback triggers.

Non-goals: full retraining of calibration models, changes to operator-level kernel implementations (out-of-scope for this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Profiling corridor emits per-layer quantiles and KV prefix norms for 95% of shadow requests with <=5% added latency overhead
Activation reconciler reduces false-positive drift alerts by >=40% on historical canary traces compared to baseline heuristic
Calibration orchestrator accepts corridor input and ranks E4M3/E5M2 candidates; top-ranked candidate passes golden-suite with <0.5% regression on heldout prompts
Canary rollout automation can safely escalate from shadow -> 1% -> 10% with defined SLO gates and automatic rollback on critical drift
Operational runbook and postmortem template added to confluence and linked in ticket
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with runtime, telemetry, and eval teams. Agreed on corridor quantiles and minimal telemetry payload schema.
2026-03-05: Prototype corridor implemented in shadow path (only metadata emitted, no storage persistence yet). Observed median activation delta under token-skew experiments.
2026-03-08: Initial reconciler algorithm (exponential smoothing + layer hysteresis) reduced noisy alerts in synthetic traces; still noisy on long-context LLM prompts.

2026-03-11: Integration spike completed: orchestrator accepts corridor JSON and produces candidate score. Golden-suite run showing candidate A passes but with a small generation fluency dip on 3/120 seeds.
2026-03-13: Telemetry team added KV norm histogram to corridor payload. Preparing canary job configuration and runbook draft.
notes: We intentionally keep telemetry payload small (<=1KB/request) to avoid spiky egress costs during high shadow-sample rates.
Fallback strategy: immediate per-request fallback to INT8/FP16 if reconciler reports sustained deviation > hysteresis window for a given layer set.
Next steps: roll synthetic perturbation sweep across production prompt buckets and iterate reconciler thresholds with telemetry team.
